docs.title: DAP Pseudocode Language
docs.text: A friendly, structured pseudocode language designed for algorithmic thinking and learning.

docs.title: What is DAP?
docs.text:
DAP is an intuitive, structured pseudocode programming language and execution environment implemented in Go. Inspired by classical computer science curricula, DAP bridges the gap between academic algorithm design and executable code.

With DAP, you can write human-readable pseudocode featuring explicit dictionary declarations, intuitive control flow, flexible array ranges, custom data structures, and functions, running them instantly with zero external dependencies.

program FactorialCalculation
dictionary
    n, result : integer
algorithm
    write "Enter a number: "
    read n

    result <- 1
    for i = 1 to n do
        {{ Calculate factorial accumulation }}
        result <- result * i
    endfor

    print "Factorial of ", n, " is ", result
endprogram

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Structured Program Layout: Explicit dictionary (declarations) and algorithm (execution) sections encourage clean variable tracking.
  • Instant Execution: Statically compiled binary with fast execution and zero external runtime dependencies.
  • Rich Type System: Primitive types (integer, real, string, char), custom structs (type < ... >), and type aliases.
  • Flexible Custom Range Arrays: Declare arrays with arbitrary index bounds like array[1..10] or array[100..200].
  • Versatile Control Flow: if-elif-else, while-do, for-to/downto-step-do, repeat-until, and depend on (switch/case).
  • Developer Tooling: Built-in interactive REPL console, token visualizer (--show-token), and Abstract Syntax Tree inspector (--show-ast).
  • Cross-Platform: Works on Windows, Linux, and macOS (Intel & Apple Silicon).

docs.title: Algorithm Examples
docs.text: Explore real-world algorithms and data manipulation patterns implemented in DAP.

docs.title: 1. Linear Search & Min-Max Finding
docs.text:
Reads integers until a sentinel value -999 is entered, finding the smallest number:

program FindMinimumNumber
dictionary
    n, minVal : integer
algorithm
    write "Enter numbers (enter -999 to stop): "
    read n
    minVal <- n

    while n != -999 do
        if n < minVal then
            minVal <- n
        endif
        read n
    endwhile

    if minVal == -999 then
        print "No numbers were entered."
    else
        print "Minimum number is: ", minVal
    endif
endprogram

docs.title: 2. Bubble Sort
docs.text:
Sorts an array of 5 integers in ascending order:

program BubbleSortExample
dictionary
    arr : array[1..5] of integer
    i, j, temp : integer
algorithm
    {{ Initialize unsorted array }}
    arr[1] <- 64
    arr[2] <- 25
    arr[3] <- 12
    arr[4] <- 22
    arr[5] <- 11

    print "Original array:"
    for i <- 1 to 5 do
        write arr[i], " "
    endfor
    print ""

    {{ Bubble sort algorithm }}
    for i <- 1 to 4 do
        for j <- 1 to (5 - i) do
            if arr[j] > arr[j + 1] then
                {{ Swap arr[j] and arr[j+1] }}
                temp <- arr[j]
                arr[j] <- arr[j + 1]
                arr[j + 1] <- temp
            endif
        endfor
    endfor

    print "Sorted array (Ascending):"
    for i <- 1 to 5 do
        write arr[i], " "
    endfor
    print ""
endprogram

docs.title: 3. Fibonacci Sequence Generator
docs.text:
Computes the first $N$ Fibonacci numbers:

program FibonacciSeries
dictionary
    n, a, b, nextVal, i : integer
algorithm
    write "How many Fibonacci numbers to generate? "
    read n

    a <- 0
    b <- 1

    print "Fibonacci Sequence:"
    for i <- 1 to n do
        print a
        nextVal <- a + b
        a <- b
        b <- nextVal
    endfor
endprogram

docs.title: 4. Temperature Conversion System
docs.text:
Uses depend on and arithmetic operations to convert temperatures between Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin:

program TemperatureConverter
dictionary
    tempC, tempF, tempK : real
    choice : integer
algorithm
    print "=== Temperature Converter ==="
    print "1. Celsius to Fahrenheit"
    print "2. Celsius to Kelvin"
    write "Select option (1-2): "
    read choice

    write "Enter temperature in Celsius: "
    read tempC

    depend on (choice)
        1:
            tempF <- (tempC * 9.0 / 5.0) + 32.0
            print tempC, " C = ", tempF, " F"
        2:
            tempK <- tempC + 273.15
            print tempC, " C = ", tempK, " K"
        default:
            print "Invalid option selected."
    enddependon
endprogram

docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text: You can install DAP via web installers, by downloading pre-compiled standalone binaries, or by compiling from source with Go.

docs.title: Windows (PowerShell)
docs.text:
Open PowerShell and run the following command:

PowerShell 
iwr -useb https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rafiathallah3/dap/main/install.ps1 | iex

docs.title: Linux & macOS (Bash / Zsh)
docs.text:
Open your terminal and run:

Bash / Zsh 
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rafiathallah3/dap/main/install.sh | bash

docs.title: Pre-compiled Binaries (GitHub Releases)
docs.text:
Download pre-compiled binaries from the GitHub Releases Page:

Operating System Architecture Package Archive Windows 64-bit (x86_64 / amd64) dap-windows-amd64.zip Linux 64-bit (x86_64 / amd64) dap-linux-amd64.tar.gz macOS Intel (x86_64) dap-darwin-amd64.tar.gz macOS Apple Silicon (arm64 / M1/M2/M3/M4) dap-darwin-arm64.tar.gz

After downloading, extract the archive and run the included install.ps1 (Windows) or ./install.sh (Linux/macOS) script to add dap to your system PATH.

docs.title: Build From Source
docs.text:
If you have Go 1.20+ installed on your machine:

  1. Clone the repository: 

    git clone https://github.com/rafiathallah3/dap.git
cd dap

  2. Run the local installer: === "Windows" 

    .\install.ps1
    === "Linux / macOS" 
    chmod +x install.sh
./install.sh

  3. Verify installation: Open a new terminal window and run: 

    dap
    If successful, you will enter the DAP interactive console.

docs.title: Quickstart Tutorial
docs.text: Learn how to write and run your first DAP program in 2 minutes.

docs.title: 1. Creating Your First File
docs.text:
Create a file named hello.dap using your preferred text editor:

program HelloWorld
dictionary
    name : string
    age  : integer
algorithm
    write "What is your name? "
    read name

    write "How old are you? "
    read age

    print "Hello, ", name, "! You are ", age, " years old."
endprogram

docs.title: 2. Running Your Program
docs.text:
Execute the file using the dap command:

dap hello.dap

docs.title: Interactive Output Example
docs.text:
What is your name? Alice
How old are you? 20
Hello, Alice! You are 20 years old.

docs.title: 3. Understanding the Anatomy
docs.text:
Every DAP program has three main structural components:

graph TD
    A["program Name"] --> B["dictionary (Declare variables, constants, types)"]
    B --> C["algorithm (Execute statements, loops, I/O)"]
    C --> D["endprogram"]
  1. program <Identifier>: Identifies the program name.
  2. dictionary: The declarative section where all variables, types, and constants must be defined.
  3. algorithm: The procedural section where your logic runs step-by-step.
  4. endprogram: Delimits the end of the program.

docs.title: 4. Trying Console (REPL) Mode
docs.text:
You can also run DAP in interactive mode by running dap without arguments:

dap

This starts the DAP REPL (Read-Eval-Print Loop) where you can quickly test expressions, statements, and logic.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: Now that you have run your first program, head over to the Program Structure Reference to explore DAP syntax and features in detail.

docs.title: CLI & Tooling Reference
docs.text: The dap binary provides tools for executing code, inspecting lexer tokens, visualizing the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST), and cross-compilation.

docs.title: Command Overview
docs.text:
Usage:
  dap [flags] [file]

Commands & Options:
  dap                       Start interactive console (REPL)
  dap <file.dap>            Execute a DAP source file
  dap --version, -v         Check DAP version and verify GitHub updates
  dap --update, -u          Automatically update DAP to latest release
  dap <file.dap> --show-token Inspect token stream from the lexer
  dap <file.dap> --show-ast   Inspect the parsed Abstract Syntax Tree
  dap <file.dap> --show-ast-json Inspect AST in JSON format
  dap --help, -h            Show help and usage information

docs.title: 1. Running Source Files
docs.text:
To execute any .dap source file:

dap program.dap

If your code contains syntax or semantic errors, DAP will print detailed error messages pointing to the exact line and column number.

docs.title: 2. Inspecting Tokens (--show-token)
docs.text:
To inspect how the DAP lexer tokenizes your program, use the --show-token flag:

dap program.dap --show-token

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
[Line 1, Col 1]  TOKEN_PROGRAM: "program"
[Line 1, Col 9]  TOKEN_IDENTIFIER: "MyProgram"
[Line 2, Col 1]  TOKEN_DICTIONARY: "dictionary"
[Line 3, Col 5]  TOKEN_IDENTIFIER: "x"
[Line 3, Col 7]  TOKEN_COLON: ":"
[Line 3, Col 9]  TOKEN_TYPE: "integer"
...

docs.title: 3. Inspecting the AST (--show-ast)
docs.text:
To view the hierarchical Abstract Syntax Tree generated by the parser:

dap program.dap --show-ast

docs.title: 4. Cross-Compiling for Other Platforms
docs.text: Since DAP is written in pure Go without CGO dependencies, you can compile it for any target operating system directly from your machine.

docs.text:

$env:GOOS="linux"; $env:GOARCH="amd64"; $env:CGO_ENABLED="0"; go build -ldflags="-s -w" -o dist/dap-linux-amd64 .

GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags="-s -w" -o dist/dap-linux-amd64 .

docs.title: Bahasa Pseudocode DAP
docs.text: Bahasa pseudocode yang terstruktur dan mudah dipahami, dirancang untuk pembelajaran logika dan perancangan algoritma.

docs.title: Apa itu DAP?
docs.text:
DAP adalah bahasa pemrograman dan interpreter pseudocode yang intuitif serta terstruktur, diimplementasikan menggunakan bahasa Go. Terinspirasi dari kurikulum dasar ilmu komputer dan algoritma perkuliahan, DAP menjembatani perancangan algoritma di atas kertas dengan kode yang dapat langsung dieksekusi di komputer.

Dengan DAP, Anda dapat menulis pseudocode dengan deklarasi kamus (dictionary) yang rapi, struktur kontrol yang intuitif, rentang array yang fleksibel, tipe bentukan (struct), serta fungsi—dan langsung menjalankannya tanpa konfigurasi yang rumit.

program HitungFaktorial
dictionary
    n, hasil : integer
algorithm
    write "Masukkan angka: "
    read n

    hasil <- 1
    for i = 1 to n do
        {{ Menghitung akumulasi faktorial }}
        hasil <- hasil * i
    endfor

    print "Faktorial dari ", n, " adalah ", hasil
endprogram

docs.title: Fitur Utama
docs.text:
• Struktur Program Teratur: Pemisahan jelas antara bagian deklarasi (dictionary) dan eksekusi (algorithm) untuk melatih kedisiplinan pelacakan variabel.
  • Eksekusi Cepat: Binary mandiri (statically compiled) dengan eksekusi instan tanpa memerlukan runtime tambahan.
  • Sistem Tipe Data Lengkap: Tipe data dasar (integer, real, string, char), tipe bentukan (type < ... >), dan alias tipe.
  • Rentang Array Fleksibel: Mendukung indeks awal dan akhir bebas, contohnya array[1..10] atau array[100..200].
  • Struktur Kontrol Lengkap: if-elif-else, while-do, for-to/downto-step-do, repeat-until, dan depend on (switch/case).
  • Alat Bantu Pengembang (CLI): Dilengkapi REPL interaktif, visualisasi token (--show-token), dan penampil Abstract Syntax Tree (--show-ast).
  • Lintas Platform: Berjalan lancar di Windows, Linux, dan macOS (Intel & Apple Silicon).

docs.title: Contoh Algoritma
docs.text: Kumpulan implementasi algoritma dan manipulasi data menggunakan bahasa DAP.

docs.title: 1. Pencarian Nilai Minimum (Linear Search / Sentinel)
docs.text:
Membaca bilangan bulat berulang kali hingga pengguna memasukkan nilai sentinel -999, lalu mencari nilai terkecil:

program CariNilaiTerkecil
dictionary
    n, palingKecil : integer
algorithm
    write "Masukkan angka (ketik -999 untuk selesai): "
    read n
    palingKecil <- n

    while n != -999 do
        if n < palingKecil then
            palingKecil <- n
        endif
        read n
    endwhile

    if palingKecil == -999 then
        print "Tidak ada angka yang dimasukkan."
    else
        print "Angka terkecil adalah: ", palingKecil
    endif
endprogram

docs.title: 2. Pengurutan Gelembung (Bubble Sort)
docs.text:
Mengurutkan array berisi 5 bilangan bulat secara menaik (ascending):

program PengurutanBubbleSort
dictionary
    arr : array[1..5] of integer
    i, j, temp : integer
algorithm
    {{ Inisialisasi data array acak }}
    arr[1] <- 64
    arr[2] <- 25
    arr[3] <- 12
    arr[4] <- 22
    arr[5] <- 11

    print "Array awal sebelum diurutkan:"
    for i <- 1 to 5 do
        write arr[i], " "
    endfor
    print ""

    {{ Algoritma Bubble Sort }}
    for i <- 1 to 4 do
        for j <- 1 to (5 - i) do
            if arr[j] > arr[j + 1] then
                {{ Tukar posisi arr[j] dan arr[j+1] }}
                temp <- arr[j]
                arr[j] <- arr[j + 1]
                arr[j + 1] <- temp
            endif
        endfor
    endfor

    print "Array setelah diurutkan (Menaik):"
    for i <- 1 to 5 do
        write arr[i], " "
    endfor
    print ""
endprogram

docs.title: 3. Pembangkit Deret Fibonacci
docs.text:
Menghasilkan $N$ bilangan pertama dari deret Fibonacci:

program PembangkitFibonacci
dictionary
    n, a, b, selanjutnya, i : integer
algorithm
    write "Berapa banyak bilangan Fibonacci yang ingin dibuat? "
    read n

    a <- 0
    b <- 1

    print "Deret Fibonacci:"
    for i <- 1 to n do
        print a
        selanjutnya <- a + b
        a <- b
        b <- selanjutnya
    endfor
endprogram

docs.title: 4. Konversi Suhu
docs.text:
Menggunakan depend on dan operasi aritmetika untuk mengubah suhu Celcius ke Fahrenheit atau Kelvin:

program KonversiSuhu
dictionary
    suhuC, suhuF, suhuK : real
    pilihan : integer
algorithm
    print "=== Sistem Konversi Suhu ==="
    print "1. Celcius ke Fahrenheit"
    print "2. Celcius ke Kelvin"
    write "Pilih menu (1-2): "
    read pilihan

    write "Masukkan nilai suhu Celcius: "
    read suhuC

    depend on (pilihan)
        1:
            suhuF <- (suhuC * 9.0 / 5.0) + 32.0
            print suhuC, " C = ", suhuF, " F"
        2:
            suhuK <- suhuC + 273.15
            print suhuC, " C = ", suhuK, " K"
        default:
            print "Pilihan menu tidak valid."
    enddependon
endprogram

docs.title: Panduan Memulai Cepat
docs.text: Pelajari cara menulis dan mengeksekusi program DAP pertama Anda dalam 2 menit.

docs.title: 1. Membuat Berkas Program Pertama
docs.text:
Buat berkas baru bernama halo.dap menggunakan text editor favorit Anda:

program HaloDunia
dictionary
    nama : string
    umur : integer
algorithm
    write "Siapa nama Anda? "
    read nama

    write "Berapa umur Anda? "
    read umur

    print "Halo, ", nama, "! Umur Anda adalah ", umur, " tahun."
endprogram

docs.title: 2. Menjalankan Program
docs.text:
Jalankan berkas tersebut menggunakan perintah dap:

dap halo.dap

docs.title: Contoh Hasil Interaksi
docs.text:
Siapa nama Anda? Budi
Berapa umur Anda? 20
Halo, Budi! Umur Anda adalah 20 tahun.

docs.title: 3. Memahami Struktur Utama
docs.text:
Setiap program DAP tersusun atas tiga komponen penting:

graph TD
    A["program NamaProgram"] --> B["dictionary (Mendeklarasikan variabel, tipe, konstanta)"]
    B --> C["algorithm (Mengeksekusi logika, perulangan, I/O)"]
    C --> D["endprogram"]
  1. program <NamaProgram>: Mendefinisikan nama program.
  2. dictionary: Bagian deklarasi tempat semua variabel, tipe, dan konstanta wajib didaftarkan sebelum digunakan.
  3. algorithm: Bagian prosedural tempat instruksi logika dieksekusi langkah demi langkah.
  4. endprogram: Penutup blok program.

docs.title: 4. Menggunakan Mode Konsol (REPL)
docs.text:
Anda juga dapat menjalankan DAP dalam mode interaktif dengan mengetikkan perintah dap tanpa argumen:

dap

Mode ini memudahkan Anda untuk menguji ekspresi matematika atau potongan kode secara langsung.

docs.title: Langkah Selanjutnya
docs.text: Setelah berhasil menjalankan program pertama Anda, lanjutkan ke Panduan Struktur Program untuk mempelajari sintaksis dan fitur lengkap DAP.

docs.title: Array & Record (Tipe Bentukan)
docs.text: DAP menyediakan struktur data majemuk: array dengan rentang indeks bebas, pengaksesan karakter string 1-indeks, dan tipe bentukan kustom (record / struct).

docs.title: 1. Array dengan Rentang Indeks Kustom
docs.text: Berbeda dengan bahasa yang membatasi indeks mulai dari 0, DAP memungkinkan Anda menentukan batas indeks awal dan akhir secara bebas (awal..akhir) sesuai dengan notasi matematika dan algoritma buku teks.

docs.title: Deklarasi Array
docs.text: namaArray : array[awal..akhir] of TipeElemen

docs.title: Contoh
docs.text:
program ContohArray
dictionary
    {{ Array 1-indeks berisi 5 integer }}
    daftarNilai : array[1..5] of integer

    {{ Array rentang tahun 2020..2025 }}
    penjualan : array[2020..2025] of real
    i : integer
algorithm
    {{ Mengisi elemen array }}
    daftarNilai[1] <- 90
    daftarNilai[2] <- 85
    daftarNilai[3] <- 95
    daftarNilai[4] <- 70
    daftarNilai[5] <- 100

    penjualan[2020] <- 150000.50
    penjualan[2021] <- 180000.75

    {{ Menampilkan isi array }}
    for i <- 1 to 5 do
        print "Nilai mahasiswa ke-", i, " = ", daftarNilai[i]
    endfor
endprogram

docs.title: 2. Pengindeksan String
docs.text:
String pada DAP dapat diakses karakternya menggunakan tanda kurung siku [ ]:

program ContohIndeksString
dictionary
    teks : string
    hurufPertama : string
algorithm
    teks <- "Algoritma"
    hurufPertama <- teks[1] {{ Menghasilkan "A" (1-indexed) }}
    print "Huruf pertama: ", hurufPertama
endprogram

docs.title: 3. Tipe Bentukan Kustom / Record (type < ... >)
docs.text: Tipe bentukan memungkinkan pengelompokan beberapa atribut dengan tipe data berbeda ke dalam satu tipe data majemuk.

docs.title: Mendefinisikan Tipe Bentukan
docs.text:
type NamaBentukan <
    field1 : tipe1
    field2 : tipe2
    ...
>

docs.title: Deklarasi & Akses Anggota Record
docs.text:
program ContohStruct
dictionary
    {{ 1. Mendefinisikan struktur record }}
    type Mahasiswa <
        nim  : integer
        nama : string
        ipk  : real
    >

    {{ 2. Mendeklarasikan variabel bertipe Mahasiswa }}
    mhs1 : Mahasiswa
algorithm
    {{ 3. Mengisi dan mengakses data menggunakan notasi titik (.) }}
    mhs1.nim <- 130121001
    mhs1.nama <- "Budi"
    mhs1.ipk <- 3.85

    print "NIM  : ", mhs1.nim
    print "Nama : ", mhs1.nama
    print "IPK  : ", mhs1.ipk
endprogram

docs.title: 4. Array dari Record (Array of Structures)
docs.text:
Anda dapat menggabungkan array dan tipe bentukan untuk mengelola koleksi data:

program ContohTabelData
dictionary
    type Produk <
        nama  : string
        harga : real
        stok  : integer
    >

    inventaris : array[1..3] of Produk
    i : integer
algorithm
    inventaris[1].nama <- "Laptop"
    inventaris[1].harga <- 9999000.0
    inventaris[1].stok <- 10

    inventaris[2].nama <- "Mouse Nirkabel"
    inventaris[2].harga <- 150000.0
    inventaris[2].stok <- 50

    inventaris[3].nama <- "Keyboard Mekanikal"
    inventaris[3].harga <- 750000.0
    inventaris[3].stok <- 30

    for i <- 1 to 3 do
        print "Produk: ", inventaris[i].nama, " | Harga: Rp", inventaris[i].harga, " | Stok: ", inventaris[i].stok
    endfor
endprogram

docs.title: Alur Kontrol
docs.text: DAP menyediakan struktur kendali alur yang lengkap: percabangan kondisi, berbagai macam perulangan, dan blok seleksi kasus (depend on).

docs.title: Bentuk Percabangan Banyak Baris
docs.text:
program PenilaianNilai
dictionary
    nilai : integer
algorithm
    read nilai

    if nilai >= 90 then
        write "Predikat A"
    elif nilai >= 80 then
        write "Predikat B"
    elif nilai >= 70 then
        write "Predikat C"
    else
        write "Predikat E"
    endif
endprogram

docs.title: Bentuk Percabangan Satu Baris
docs.text: if x < 0 then x <- -x

docs.title: 2. Perulangan While (while ... do ... endwhile)
docs.text:
Mengulang serangkaian instruksi selama kondisi evaluasi bernilai true.

program ContohWhile
dictionary
    pencacah : integer
algorithm
    pencacah <- 1
    while pencacah <= 5 do
        print "Hitungan: ", pencacah
        pencacah <- pencacah + 1
    endwhile
endprogram

docs.title: 3. Perulangan For (for ... to / downto ... step ... do)
docs.text: Perulangan for pada DAP sangat intuitif dan mudah dibaca:

docs.title: Penaikan Standar (to)
docs.text:
for i <- 1 to 10 do
    print i
endfor

docs.title: Kelipatan Langkah Kustom (step)
docs.text:
{{ Langkah per 2: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 }}
for i <- 0 to 10 step 2 do
    print i
endfor

docs.title: Perulangan Menurun (downto)
docs.text:
{{ Hitung mundur: 10, 9, 8 ... 1 }}
for i <- 10 downto 1 do
    print "Hitung Mundur: ", i
endfor

docs.title: 4. Perulangan Repeat-Until (repeat ... until)
docs.text:
Perulangan dengan pemeriksaan kondisi di akhir. Blok instruksi dieksekusi minimal satu kali dan terus berjalan sampai kondisi menjadi true.

program ContohRepeatUntil
dictionary
    angka : integer
algorithm
    angka <- 1
    repeat
        print "Nilai: ", angka
        angka <- angka * 2
    until angka > 50
endprogram

docs.title: 5. Seleksi Kasus (depend on ... enddependon)
docs.text: DAP mendukung dua pola penulisan blok depend on:

docs.title: Pola 1: Pencocokan Nilai Variabel
docs.text:
depend on (nomorHari)
    1 : print "Senin"
    2 : print "Selasa"
    3 : print "Rabu"
    default : print "Hari lainnya"
enddependon

docs.title: Pola 2: Pencocokan Kondisi / Ekspresi
docs.text:
depend on
    nilai >= 90 : print "Sangat Memuaskan"
    nilai >= 75 : print "Baik"
    nilai >= 50 : print "Cukup"
    default : print "Perlu Perbaikan"
enddependon

docs.title: Fungsi & Subrutin
docs.text: Fungsi pada DAP memungkinkan pengorganisasian kode modular yang dapat digunakan berulang kali dengan penerimaan argumen dan nilai kembalian.

docs.title: 1. Definisi Fungsi Banyak Baris
docs.text:
Mendefinisikan fungsi banyak baris menggunakan sintaksis function <nama>(argumen) ... end:

program ContohFungsi
dictionary
    a, b, nilaiMaks : integer

    {{ Definisi fungsi }}
    function cariMaks(x, y)
        if x > y then
            return x
        else
            return y
        endif
    end
algorithm
    a <- 42
    b <- 99
    nilaiMaks <- cariMaks(a, b)
    print "Nilai maksimum adalah: ", nilaiMaks
endprogram

docs.title: 2. Fungsi Sebaris (Inline Arrow Function)
docs.text:
Untuk ekspresi matematika atau transformasi sederhana, gunakan sintaksis panah ->:

program ContohFungsiSebaris
dictionary
    angka, duaKali, kuadrat : integer

    function kaliDua(n) -> n * 2
    function pangkatDua(n) -> n ^ 2
algorithm
    angka <- 5
    duaKali <- kaliDua(angka)
    kuadrat <- pangkatDua(angka)

    print "Angka: ", angka
    print "Hasil Kali Dua: ", duaKali
    print "Hasil Pangkat Dua: ", kuadrat
endprogram

docs.title: 3. Pernyataan Kendali Fungsi & Perulangan
docs.text: DAP menyediakan kata kunci pengendalian eksekusi:

docs.title: return [ekspresi]
docs.text: Menghentikan eksekusi fungsi yang sedang berjalan dan mengembalikan nilai ke pemanggil.

docs.title: break
docs.text:
Menghentikan paksa perulangan terdalam (for, while, atau repeat).

for i <- 1 to 100 do
    if i == 5 then
        break {{ Hentikan perulangan saat i mencapai 5 }}
    endif
    print i
endfor

docs.title: continue
docs.text:
Melewati sisa perintah pada iterasi saat ini dan langsung melompat ke iterasi berikutnya.

for i <- 1 to 10 do
    if i % 2 == 0 then
        continue {{ Lewati bilangan genap }}
    endif
    print "Bilangan ganjil: ", i
endfor

docs.title: Masukan & Keluaran (I/O)
docs.text: DAP menyediakan instruksi dasar untuk membaca data dari pengguna dan mencetak hasil ke layar konsol.

docs.title: 1. Menampilkan Keluaran (write / print)
docs.text: DAP mendukung kata kunci write dan print (serta huruf besar WRITE dan PRINT).

docs.title: Sintaksis
docs.text:
write ekspresi1, ekspresi2, ...
print(ekspresi1, ekspresi2, ...)

docs.title: Contoh
docs.text:
program ContohKeluaran
dictionary
    nilai : real
    namaPemain : string
algorithm
    namaPemain <- "Rafi"
    nilai <- 95.5

    {{ Mencetak teks biasa }}
    print "Selamat datang di DAP!"

    {{ Mencetak beberapa variabel dan teks sekaligus }}
    write "Pemain: ", namaPemain, " | Nilai: ", nilai

    {{ Mencetak hasil evaluasi ekspresi }}
    print "Target nilai berikutnya: ", nilai + 10.0
endprogram

docs.title: 2. Membaca Masukan (read / input)
docs.text: Membaca nilai masukan dari pengguna melalui standar masukan (stdin). Kata kunci read dan input (tidak peka huruf besar/kecil) didukung secara penuh.

docs.title: Sintaksis
docs.text:
read namaVariabel
input(namaVariabel)

docs.title: Contoh
docs.text:
program ContohMasukan
dictionary
    umur : integer
    gaji : real
    nama : string
algorithm
    write "Masukkan nama Anda: "
    read nama

    write "Masukkan umur Anda: "
    read umur

    write "Masukkan estimasi gaji: "
    read gaji

    print "Ringkasan Profil: ", nama, ", ", umur, " tahun, gaji: Rp", gaji
endprogram

[!NOTE] DAP secara otomatis mengonversi string masukan menjadi tipe data target variabel yang sesuai (seperti mengonversi teks angka menjadi bilangan bulat atau pecahan saat membaca variabel integer atau real).

docs.title: Operator & Ekspresi
docs.text: DAP menyediakan kumpulan operator aritmetika, perbandingan, penugasan, dan logika yang lengkap.

docs.title: 1. Operator Penugasan (Assignment)
docs.text:
Operator Sintaksis Deskripsi Contoh <- x <- nilai Simbol penugasan utama (panah kiri) total <- 100 = x = nilai Simbol penugasan standar total = 100

[!TIP] Dalam penulisan pseudocode DAP yang baku, simbol <- sangat dianjurkan agar berbeda jelas dengan operator pembanding kesetaraan (==). Operator penugasan majemuk (seperti += atau *=) tidak digunakan dalam DAP standar; gunakan bentuk ekspansi jelas (x <- x + 1).

docs.title: 2. Operator Aritmetika
docs.text: Operator Nama Penjelasan Contoh Hasil + Penjumlahan / Penggabungan Jumlah angka atau gabung teks 5 + 3 atau "Halo " + "Dunia" 8 atau "Halo Dunia" - Pengurangan / Negasi Selisih nilai atau nilai minus 10 - 4 atau -x 6 * Perkalian Mengalikan dua bilangan 4 * 3 12 / Pembagian Real Pembagian desimal/pecahan 7 / 2 3.5 div / DIV Pembagian Bulat Pembagian bilangan bulat (tanpa sisa) 7 div 2 3 % Modulo Sisa hasil bagi 7 % 3 1 ^ Pemangkatan Pangkat bilangan 2 ^ 3 8

docs.title: 3. Operator Perbandingan (Relasional)
docs.text:
Operator perbandingan membandingkan dua ekspresi dan mengembalikan nilai kebenaran (true atau false):

Operator Deskripsi Contoh Hasil jika a=5, b=10 == Sama dengan a == b false != Tidak sama dengan a != b true < Kurang dari a < b true <= Kurang dari atau sama dengan a <= 5 true > Lebih dari a > b false >= Lebih dari atau sama dengan b >= 10 true

docs.title: 4. Operator Logika
docs.text:
Operator logika menggabungkan dua atau lebih kondisi boolean:

Operator Nama Deskripsi Contoh && Logika DAN (AND) Menghasilkan true jika kedua kondisi bernilai benar (x > 0) && (x < 100) \|\| Logika ATAU (OR) Menghasilkan true jika salah satu kondisi bernilai benar (a == 0) \|\| (b == 0) ! Logika BUKAN (NOT) Membalik nilai kebenaran suatu kondisi !(x == 10)

docs.title: 5. Prioritas Operator (Precedence)
docs.text:
Urutan evaluasi operator dari prioritas tertinggi ke terendah:

  1. Tanda kurung: ( ... )
  2. Akses anggota record / elemen array: ., [ ]
  3. Pemangkatan: ^
  4. Unary: -, !
  5. Perkalian & pembagian: *, /, div, %
  6. Penjumlahan & pengurangan: +, -
  7. Relasional: <, <=, >, >=
  8. Kesetaraan: ==, !=
  9. Logika DAN: &&
  10. Logika ATAU: ||
  11. Penugasan: <-, =

docs.title: Struktur Program & Tata Letak
docs.text: Setiap program DAP mengikuti struktur yang rapi dan disiplin, terinspirasi dari tata cara penulisan pseudocode algoritma perkuliahan.

docs.title: Format Standar Program
docs.text:
Berkas sumber DAP terdiri atas tiga bagian utama:

program <NamaProgram>
dictionary
    {{ 1. Deklarasi (Tipe bentukan, Variabel, Konstanta) }}
algorithm
    {{ 2. Pernyataan eksekusi (Logika, Perulangan, I/O) }}
endprogram

docs.title: Penjelasan Bagian Program
docs.text:
1. program <NamaProgram>
  2. Wajib menjadi pernyataan pertama di awal berkas.

  3. <NamaProgram> adalah sebuah pengenal/identifier (misalnya DeretFibonacci, Kalkulator).

  4. Bagian dictionary (Kamus)

  5. Semua variabel, tipe bentukan (struct), konstanta, dan alias tipe wajib dideklarasikan di bagian ini.

  6. Variabel yang digunakan pada bagian algorithm namun belum terdaftar di dictionary akan memicu galat semantik (compile error).

  7. Bagian algorithm (Algoritma)

  8. Berisi seluruh logika prosedural dan struktur kontrol program.

  9. Penugasan variabel, percabangan, perulangan, definisi fungsi, dan perintah masukan/keluaran diletakkan di sini.

  10. endprogram

  11. Menandai akhir dari program.

docs.title: Komentar
docs.text:
Pada DAP, komentar ditulis di dalam kurung kurawal: {{ komentar }} atau { komentar }.

{{ Ini adalah contoh komentar di DAP }}
x <- 10 {{ Komentar di ujung baris }}

[!NOTE] Semua teks di dalam { ... } dan {{ ... }} akan diabaikan oleh lexer saat proses tokenisasi.

docs.title: Kata Kunci Penutup Blok
docs.text:
DAP mendukung penutup blok spesifik maupun kata kunci umum end:

Jenis Blok Penutup Spesifik Penutup Umum Program endprogram - If / Elif endif end Perulangan While endwhile end Perulangan For endfor end Perulangan Repeat until <kondisi> - Depend on (Switch) enddependon end Fungsi end / endif end

docs.title: Tipe Data, Variabel & Konstanta
docs.text: Semua tipe data dan variabel pada DAP wajib dideklarasikan di dalam blok dictionary sebelum digunakan pada bagian algorithm.

docs.title: 1. Tipe Data Primitif
docs.text:
DAP menyediakan empat tipe data dasar dengan nilai awal (zero-value) yang terdefinisi jelas:

Tipe Data Deskripsi Nilai Default Contoh Nilai integer Bilangan bulat bertanda (64-bit) 0 0, 42, -15 real Bilangan pecahan / desimal (float) 0.0 3.14, -0.5, 100.0 string Teks rangkaian karakter (UTF-8) "" "Halo", "Pseudocode DAP" char Karakter tunggal " " (spasi) "a", "Z", "9"

docs.title: 2. Deklarasi Variabel
docs.text:
Variabel dideklarasikan dengan pola: namaVariabel : TipeData atau daftar dipisahkan koma var1, var2 : TipeData.

program ContohVariabel
dictionary
    {{ Deklarasi variabel tunggal }}
    jumlah : integer
    nilai  : real
    pesan  : string

    {{ Deklarasi banyak variabel sekaligus }}
    x, y, z : integer
    namaDepan, namaBelakang : string
algorithm
    x <- 10
    y <- 20
    z <- x + y
    print z
endprogram

docs.title: 3. Konstanta (const)
docs.text:
Konstanta adalah nilai tetap yang tidak dapat diubah atau ditugaskan kembali di mana pun dalam program.

Format: const namaKonstanta = nilai atau const namaKonstanta <- nilai

program ContohKonstanta
dictionary
    const PI = 3.14159
    const MAKS_PENGGUNA = 100
    const NAMA_APLIKASI = "Mesin DAP"

    radius : real
    luas   : real
algorithm
    radius <- 5.0
    luas <- PI * (radius ^ 2)
    print "Luas Lingkaran: ", luas
endprogram

[!WARNING] Mencoba mengubah nilai variabel const di dalam bagian algorithm (misalnya PI <- 3.0) akan memicu galat semantik saat kompilasi.

docs.title: 4. Alias Tipe (type)
docs.text:
Anda dapat membuat nama kustom untuk tipe data yang sudah ada menggunakan sintaksis type NamaAlias : TipeTujuan:

program ContohAliasTipe
dictionary
    type Pecahan : real
    type Umur : integer

    umurSaya : Umur
    harga    : Pecahan
algorithm
    umurSaya <- 21
    harga <- 99.99
    print "Umur: ", umurSaya, ", Harga: Rp", harga
endprogram

docs.title: Arrays & Structures
docs.text: DAP provides composite data structures: custom-range arrays, 1-indexed string access, and user-defined records (structures).

docs.title: 1. Custom-Range Arrays
docs.text: Unlike languages constrained strictly to 0-indexing, DAP lets you define arbitrary index bounds (start..end) matching mathematical and algorithmic specifications.

docs.title: Array Declaration
docs.text: arrayName : array[start..end] of ElementType

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
program ArrayExample
dictionary
    {{ 1-indexed array of 5 integers }}
    scores : array[1..5] of integer

    {{ Custom offset array (e.g. tracking years 2020..2025) }}
    sales : array[2020..2025] of real
    i : integer
algorithm
    {{ Assigning elements }}
    scores[1] <- 90
    scores[2] <- 85
    scores[3] <- 95
    scores[4] <- 70
    scores[5] <- 100

    sales[2020] <- 150000.50
    sales[2021] <- 180000.75

    {{ Iterating over the array }}
    for i <- 1 to 5 do
        print "Student ", i, " score = ", scores[i]
    endfor
endprogram

docs.title: 2. String Indexing
docs.text:
Strings in DAP can be indexed directly to read individual characters:

program StringIndexDemo
dictionary
    str : string
    firstChar : string
algorithm
    str <- "Algorithm"
    firstChar <- str[1] {{ Returns "A" (1-indexed) }}
    print "First character: ", firstChar
endprogram

docs.title: 3. Custom Structures (type < ... >)
docs.text: Structures allow you to group related fields of different data types into a single composite type.

docs.title: Defining a Struct Type
docs.text:
type StructName <
    field1 : type1
    field2 : type2
    ...
>

docs.title: Declaring & Accessing Struct Variables
docs.text:
program StructDemo
dictionary
    {{ 1. Define struct layout }}
    type Student <
        id    : integer
        name  : string
        gpa   : real
    >

    {{ 2. Declare variables of this type }}
    student1 : Student
algorithm
    {{ 3. Access and mutate fields using dot notation (.) }}
    student1.id <- 101
    student1.name <- "Alice"
    student1.gpa <- 3.92

    print "ID: ", student1.id
    print "Name: ", student1.name
    print "GPA: ", student1.gpa
endprogram

docs.title: 4. Arrays of Structures
docs.text:
Combine arrays and structures to model collections of complex records:

program ArrayOfStructsDemo
dictionary
    type Product <
        name  : string
        price : real
        stock : integer
    >

    inventory : array[1..3] of Product
    i : integer
algorithm
    inventory[1].name <- "Laptop"
    inventory[1].price <- 999.99
    inventory[1].stock <- 10

    inventory[2].name <- "Wireless Mouse"
    inventory[2].price <- 25.50
    inventory[2].stock <- 50

    inventory[3].name <- "Mechanical Keyboard"
    inventory[3].price <- 75.00
    inventory[3].stock <- 30

    for i <- 1 to 3 do
        print "Product: ", inventory[i].name, " | Price: $", inventory[i].price, " | Stock: ", inventory[i].stock
    endfor
endprogram

docs.title: Control Flow
docs.text: DAP supports comprehensive control flow structures: branching conditions, multiple loop formats, and pattern-matching switch blocks.

docs.title: Multi-line If-Elif-Else
docs.text:
program GradeEvaluation
dictionary
    score : integer
algorithm
    read score

    if score >= 90 then
        write "Grade A"
    elif score >= 80 then
        write "Grade B"
    elif score >= 70 then
        write "Grade C"
    else
        write "Grade F"
    endif
endprogram

docs.title: Single-line Short If
docs.text: if x < 0 then x <- -x

docs.title: 2. While Loop (while ... do ... endwhile)
docs.text:
Repeats statements as long as the condition evaluates to true.

program WhileDemo
dictionary
    counter : integer
algorithm
    counter <- 1
    while counter <= 5 do
        print "Count: ", counter
        counter <- counter + 1
    endwhile
endprogram

docs.title: 3. For Loop (for ... to / downto ... step ... do)
docs.text: The for loop in DAP is flexible and intuitive:

docs.title: Standard Increment (to)
docs.text:
for i <- 1 to 10 do
    print i
endfor

docs.title: Custom Step (step)
docs.text:
{{ Step by 2: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 }}
for i <- 0 to 10 step 2 do
    print i
endfor

docs.title: Decrementing Loop (downto)
docs.text:
{{ Counts down: 10, 9, 8 ... 1 }}
for i <- 10 downto 1 do
    print "Countdown: ", i
endfor

docs.title: 4. Repeat-Until Loop (repeat ... until)
docs.text:
A post-tested loop that runs the body at least once and continues executing until the condition becomes true.

program RepeatUntilDemo
dictionary
    num : integer
algorithm
    num <- 1
    repeat
        print "Value: ", num
        num <- num * 2
    until num > 50
endprogram

docs.title: 5. Switch-Case (depend on ... enddependon)
docs.text: DAP provides two styles for depend on blocks:

docs.title: Style 1: Value Matching
docs.text:
depend on (dayNumber)
    1 : print "Monday"
    2 : print "Tuesday"
    3 : print "Wednesday"
    default : print "Other day"
enddependon

docs.title: Style 2: Expression / Condition Matching
docs.text:
depend on
    score >= 90 : print "Excellent"
    score >= 75 : print "Good"
    score >= 50 : print "Passing"
    default : print "Needs Improvement"
enddependon

docs.title: Functions & Subroutines
docs.text: Functions in DAP allow you to structure reusable logic with parameter passing and return values.

docs.title: 1. Multi-line Function Definition
docs.text:
Define multi-line functions with function <name>(args) ... end:

program FunctionExample
dictionary
    a, b, maxVal : integer

    {{ Function definition }}
    function findMax(x, y)
        if x > y then
            return x
        else
            return y
        endif
    end
algorithm
    a <- 42
    b <- 99
    maxVal <- findMax(a, b)
    print "The maximum value is: ", maxVal
endprogram

docs.title: 2. Inline Arrow Functions
docs.text:
For concise mathematical expressions or transformations, use the arrow -> syntax:

program InlineFunctionExample
dictionary
    num, doubled, squared : integer

    function doubleVal(n) -> n * 2
    function squareVal(n) -> n ^ 2
algorithm
    num <- 5
    doubled <- doubleVal(num)
    squared <- squareVal(num)

    print "Number: ", num
    print "Doubled: ", doubled
    print "Squared: ", squared
endprogram

docs.title: 3. Control Flow Statements in Functions & Loops
docs.text: DAP supports standard subroutine and loop control keywords:

docs.title: return [expression]
docs.text: Exits the current function and optionally returns a value back to the caller.

docs.title: break
docs.text:
Immediately terminates the innermost active loop (for, while, or repeat).

for i <- 1 to 100 do
    if i == 5 then
        break {{ Stop the loop when i reaches 5 }}
    endif
    print i
endfor

docs.title: continue
docs.text:
Skips the remainder of the current iteration and proceeds to the next cycle.

for i <- 1 to 10 do
    if i % 2 == 0 then
        continue {{ Skip even numbers }}
    endif
    print "Odd number: ", i
endfor

docs.title: Input & Output
docs.text: DAP provides built-in primitives for console input and output.

docs.title: 1. Output Statements (write / print)
docs.text: DAP supports both write and print keywords (as well as uppercase WRITE and PRINT).

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
write expression1, expression2, ...
print(expression1, expression2, ...)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
program OutputDemo
dictionary
    score : real
    player : string
algorithm
    player <- "Rafi"
    score <- 95.5

    {{ Basic print }}
    print "Welcome to DAP!"

    {{ Multiple comma-separated arguments }}
    write "Player: ", player, " | Score: ", score

    {{ Expressions evaluated on the fly }}
    print "Next level target: ", score + 10.0
endprogram

docs.title: 2. Input Statements (read / input)
docs.text: Read user input directly from standard input (stdin) into variables. Both read and input keywords (case-insensitive) are supported.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
read variableName
input(variableName)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
program InputDemo
dictionary
    userAge : integer
    salary  : real
    name    : string
algorithm
    write "Enter your name: "
    read name

    write "Enter your age: "
    read userAge

    write "Enter your desired salary: "
    read salary

    print "Profile Summary: ", name, ", ", userAge, " years old, salary: ", salary
endprogram

[!NOTE] DAP automatically converts input strings to the appropriate target variable type (e.g. parsing integer or real numbers when reading into numeric variables).

docs.title: Operators & Expressions
docs.text: DAP provides a complete suite of arithmetic, comparison, assignment, and logical operators.

docs.title: 1. Assignment Operators
docs.text:
Operator Syntax Description Example <- x <- val Preferred arrow assignment total <- 100 = x = val Standard assignment total = 100

[!TIP] In idiomatic DAP pseudocode, <- is the recommended assignment symbol to clearly distinguish assignment from equality comparisons (==). Compound assignment operators (like += or *=) are not used in standard DAP; use explicit expansion (x <- x + 1).

docs.title: 2. Arithmetic Operators
docs.text: Operator Name Behavior Example Result + Addition / Concatenation Numeric sum or string joining 5 + 3 or "Hello " + "World" 8 or "Hello World" - Subtraction / Negation Difference or unary negative 10 - 4 or -x 6 * Multiplication Multiplies two numbers 4 * 3 12 / Real Division Performs floating-point division 7 / 2 3.5 div / DIV Integer Division Truncates decimal part 7 div 2 3 % Modulo Remainder of division 7 % 3 1 ^ Exponentiation Raises to power 2 ^ 3 8

docs.title: 3. Comparison Operators
docs.text:
Comparison operators evaluate expressions and return boolean values (true or false):

Operator Description Example Result for a=5, b=10 == Equal to a == b false != Not equal to a != b true < Less than a < b true <= Less than or equal to a <= 5 true > Greater than a > b false >= Greater than or equal to b >= 10 true

docs.title: 4. Logical Operators
docs.text:
Logical operators combine boolean expressions:

Operator Name Description Example && Logical AND Returns true only if both operands are true (x > 0) && (x < 100) \|\| Logical OR Returns true if at least one operand is true (a == 0) \|\| (b == 0) ! Logical NOT Inverts the boolean truth value !(x == 10)

docs.title: 5. Operator Precedence
docs.text:
From highest precedence to lowest:

  1. Parentheses: ( ... )
  2. Member / Array access: ., [ ]
  3. Exponentiation: ^
  4. Unary: -, !
  5. Multiplicative: *, /, div, %
  6. Additive: +, -
  7. Relational: <, <=, >, >=
  8. Equality: ==, !=
  9. Logical AND: &&
  10. Logical OR: ||
  11. Assignment: <-, =

docs.title: Program Structure & Layout
docs.text: Every DAP program follows a clear, disciplined structure inspired by classical computer science pseudocode.

docs.title: The Standard Template
docs.text:
A DAP source file consists of three mandatory parts:

program <ProgramName>
dictionary
    {{ 1. Declarations (Types, Variables, Constants) }}
algorithm
    {{ 2. Executable statements (Logic, Loops, I/O) }}
endprogram

docs.title: Sections Explained
docs.text:
1. program <ProgramName>
  2. Must be the first statement of the file.

  3. <ProgramName> is an identifier (e.g. FibonacciSequence, Calculator).

  4. dictionary Section

  5. All variables, custom struct types, constants, and type aliases must be declared here.

  6. Undeclared variables used in the algorithm section will raise a compile-time semantic error.

  7. algorithm Section

  8. Contains all procedural and control flow logic.

  9. Variable assignments, loop constructs, conditionals, function definitions, and I/O statements are written here.

  10. endprogram

  11. Marks the termination of the program.

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
In DAP, comments are enclosed using curly braces: {{ comment }} or { comment }.

{{ This is a comment in DAP }}
x <- 10 {{ This is an inline comment }}

[!NOTE] The lexer skips everything inside curly braces { ... } and {{ ... }} during tokenization.

docs.title: Block Terminators
docs.text:
DAP supports both specific end keywords and generic end keywords for readability:

Block Type Specific Ending Generic Ending Program endprogram - If / Elif endif end While loop endwhile end For loop endfor end Repeat loop until <condition> - Depend on (Switch) enddependon end Function end / endif end

docs.title: Types, Variables & Constants
docs.text: All data types and variables in DAP must be declared inside the dictionary block before being utilized in the algorithm block.

docs.title: 1. Primitive Data Types
docs.text:
DAP provides four foundational primitive data types with predictable default zero-values:

Type Description Default Value Example Literals integer 64-bit signed integer 0 0, 42, -15 real Floating-point real number 0.0 3.14, -0.5, 100.0 string UTF-8 string text "" "Hello", "DAP Pseudocode" char Single character " " (space) "a", "Z", "9"

docs.title: 2. Variable Declarations
docs.text:
Variables are declared with the format: name : Type or comma-separated lists var1, var2 : Type.

program VariableDemo
dictionary
    {{ Single variable declarations }}
    count : integer
    score : real
    message : string

    {{ Multi-variable declarations }}
    x, y, z : integer
    firstName, lastName : string
algorithm
    x <- 10
    y <- 20
    z <- x + y
    print z
endprogram

docs.title: 3. Constants (const)
docs.text:
Constants are fixed values that cannot be reassigned or modified anywhere in the program.

Format: const name = value or const name <- value

program ConstantDemo
dictionary
    const PI = 3.14159
    const MAX_USERS = 100
    const APP_NAME = "DAP Engine"

    radius : real
    area   : real
algorithm
    radius <- 5.0
    area <- PI * (radius ^ 2)
    print "Area: ", area
endprogram

[!WARNING] Attempting to reassign a const variable inside the algorithm section (e.g. PI <- 3.0) will trigger a compile-time semantic error.

docs.title: 4. Type Aliases
docs.text:
You can define custom names for existing types using the type AliasName : TargetType syntax:

program TypeAliasDemo
dictionary
    type Float : real
    type Age : integer

    myAge : Age
    price : Float
algorithm
    myAge <- 21
    price <- 99.99
    print "Age: ", myAge, ", Price: $", price
endprogram
